ops.content: The brain daemon restart protocol now routes through `launchctl kickstart -k` rather than a direct Popen spawn. To restart the daemon, invoke `launchctl kickstart -k <service-target>` (where the service target identifies the brain daemon's launchd job). This replaces the previous approach of spawning the process directly, ensuring launchd owns the process lifecycle, handles restarts cleanly, and avoids orphaned processes.

ops.reason: Architecture changed June 2026: restarts now route through launchctl kickstart -k, not a direct Popen spawn.
ops.content: Daemon restarts are issued via `launchctl kickstart -k <service-target>` rather than a direct Popen spawn. The `-k` flag kills any running instance before relaunching, ensuring a clean restart. The launchctl route delegates process lifecycle to launchd, which owns the service socket and environment, avoiding the fd-leak and orphan-process issues that could arise from spawning a child directly.

ops.reason: Architecture changed June 2026: restarts now route through launchctl kickstart -k, not direct Popen spawn.
ops.content: The brain daemon restart protocol now routes through `launchctl kickstart -k` rather than a direct `Popen` spawn. When a restart is needed, the controlling process issues `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<UID>/com.brain.daemon` (or the relevant service label), which causes launchctl to tear down the existing job and immediately re-launch it under the correct launchd context. This replaces the previous approach of directly spawning the daemon process via `Popen`, which bypassed launchd supervision and could leave the service in an inconsistent state.

When a restart is needed, the MCP layer invokes `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<uid>/com.brain.daemon` (or the equivalent service target), which causes launchd to tear down the existing daemon process and immediately relaunch it under proper supervision. The old direct-spawn path (Popen of the daemon binary) is no longer used and should not be invoked — it bypasses launchd supervision and will result in two competing daemon processes.

ops.reason: Architecture changed June 2026: restarts now route through launchctl kickstart -k, not direct Popen spawn.
ops.content: The brain daemon restart protocol now routes through `launchctl kickstart -k` instead of a direct Popen spawn. When a restart is required, the caller issues `launchctl kickstart -k <service-target>`, which causes launchd to atomically stop and re-launch the daemon under its managed service definition. This ensures the process is owned and supervised by launchd rather than being an orphaned child of the invoking process, and avoids fd-leak and signal-handling edge cases that affected the old Popen path.

ops.title: WAL checkpoint starvation under parallel sessions
ops.content: When two sessions write concurrently, the TRUNCATE checkpoint starves; symptom is an ever-growing -wal file.

connect_to.why: Checkpoint starvation is caused by writer-slot contention: when concurrent sessions hold the WAL writer slot, the TRUNCATE checkpoint cannot complete, producing an ever-growing -wal file.
